# Check catalog

<!-- Generated by `probe checks list --format md`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Probe ships 23 checks. Each runs in a fixed phase, is judged by what the
server does, and reports PASS, FAIL, NOT_APPLICABLE, SKIPPED or ERROR. Severity here is
the catalog severity, which sets the check's weight; an individual finding may be
reported at a different level.

## Details

### schema.cache_ttl_sane

**Cache lifetimes are not absurdly long**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** A list cached for longer than a day will outlive the tools it describes, so clients keep calling tools that changed or are gone.

**How to fix.** Use a ttlMs of at most 24 hours (86400000) for list results.

### schema.descriptions_present

**Tools and their required parameters are described**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Models choose tools and fill arguments from descriptions. Undescribed tools and required parameters are guessed at.

**How to fix.** Give every tool a description and every required parameter a description.

### schema.input_schema_strict

**Input schemas are strict (information only)**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Schemas that forbid extra properties and list required ones reject malformed calls early. Loose ones accept whatever a model invents.

**How to fix.** Set "additionalProperties": false and list required parameters.

### schema.input_schema_valid

**Every inputSchema is a valid JSON Schema with an object root**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Clients build forms and validate arguments from inputSchema. An invalid schema cannot be used, and a non-object root cannot describe named arguments.

**How to fix.** Publish a valid JSON Schema (2020-12 unless $schema says otherwise) whose root has "type": "object".

### schema.refs_resolvable

**Schema references resolve inside the schema**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** A $ref that points nowhere makes the schema unusable. A remote $ref makes clients fetch URLs the server chose, which leaks requests and invites SSRF.

**How to fix.** Inline remote definitions under $defs and make every $ref point inside the schema.

### schema.tool_names_valid

**Tool names are well formed and unique**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool-names

**Why it matters.** Names are identifiers clients show, route on and put in headers. Odd characters or duplicates make tools unreachable or ambiguous.

**How to fix.** Use unique names of 1-128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, dash and dot.

### schema.tools_list_valid

**tools/list results conform to the protocol schema**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools

**Why it matters.** Clients parse tools/list with the official schema. A tool without inputSchema or a result with the wrong shape breaks every client that validates strictly.

**How to fix.** Return tools/list results that validate against the version's schema.json.

### schema.x_mcp_header_valid

**x-mcp-header annotations obey their constraints**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters

**Why it matters.** Clients mirror annotated parameters into HTTP headers and must drop tools whose annotations are invalid, so a bad annotation makes the tool unavailable over HTTP.

**How to fix.** Annotate only string, integer or boolean parameters reachable through properties, with unique token-syntax names.

### protocol.deprecated_features

**Uses of deprecated MCP features**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/deprecated

**Why it matters.** Deprecated features stay in the spec for a while and then go away. Knowing which ones a server relies on tells its maintainers what to migrate.

**How to fix.** Follow the migration paths in the deprecated features registry.

### protocol.discover_implemented

**server/discover is implemented and well formed**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/discover

**Why it matters.** Clients detect a server's era and supported versions with server/discover. A modern-capable server without it looks like a legacy server and is driven with the wrong protocol.

**How to fix.** Implement server/discover and return supportedVersions, capabilities, resultType, ttlMs and cacheScope.

### protocol.era_parity

**A dual-era server offers the same tools in both eras**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: second_instance
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions

**Why it matters.** A server that answers both eras should be one server. If a client's era changes which tools or schemas it sees, behavior depends on how the client connected.

**How to fix.** Serve the same tool names and schemas to modern and legacy clients.

### protocol.unknown_method_error

**An unknown method is answered with -32601**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#error_object, 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages-to-the-server

**Why it matters.** Clients probe for optional methods and rely on -32601 to learn a feature is absent. Any other answer makes feature detection unreliable.

**How to fix.** Answer unknown methods with error -32601 (Method not found); over modern HTTP also use status 404.

### protocol.unsupported_version_error

**An unsupported protocol version is rejected with -32022**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation

**Why it matters.** There is no handshake: a client learns which versions a server speaks from the error to a request with a version it does not support. Without the right error clients cannot recover.

**How to fix.** Reject unsupported versions with code -32022 (HTTP 400) and data.supported listing your versions and data.requested echoing the version that was sent.

### schema.cache_scope_correct

**Lists that differ between users are not marked public**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: auth_identities
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** cacheScope "public" lets a shared cache or gateway store a result once and serve it to everybody. If the list depends on who asks, one user's tools or resources are shown to another.

**How to fix.** Mark any list that depends on the caller's identity or permissions with cacheScope "private".

### schema.tool_order_deterministic

**tools/list returns the same tools in the same order every time**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools

**Why it matters.** A shuffled or changing tool list breaks pagination, caching and prompt caching for models, and makes the server's behavior hard to reproduce.

**How to fix.** Return tools in a stable order (for example sorted by name) with stable content.

### protocol.header_mismatch_rejected

**Headers that disagree with the request body are rejected**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#server-validation

**Why it matters.** Gateways route and authorize on the Mcp-Method and version headers. If the server trusts the body when the headers disagree, a proxy can be tricked into applying the policy of one method to another.

**How to fix.** Compare Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name and MCP-Protocol-Version with the body and answer a mismatch with HTTP 400 and error -32020.

### protocol.malformed_jsonrpc_handled

**Malformed JSON-RPC input gets an error and does not hurt the server**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#error_object

**Why it matters.** Any client or attacker can send garbage. A server must answer it with a JSON-RPC error and keep serving; one that hangs or dies on bad input can be taken down by it.

**How to fix.** Return -32700 for unparseable JSON and -32600 for an invalid request (HTTP 400), and never let a malformed message crash or wedge the server.

### protocol.origin_validated

**A request from an untrusted Origin is rejected**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-warning

**Why it matters.** Without Origin validation a web page the user visits can call a locally running MCP server (DNS rebinding) and use its tools with the user's authority.

**How to fix.** Validate the Origin header on every request and reject a present but untrusted origin with HTTP 403; bind local servers to 127.0.0.1.

### protocol.required_headers_enforced

**Requests missing the required headers are rejected**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#request-metadata

**Why it matters.** MCP-Protocol-Version and Mcp-Method are required so intermediaries can route without parsing bodies. A server that accepts requests without them makes those intermediaries unreliable.

**How to fix.** Reject requests without MCP-Protocol-Version or Mcp-Method with HTTP 400.

### protocol.error_code_ranges

**Error codes stay inside the ranges the spec allows**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#errors

**Why it matters.** -32020 to -32099 belong to the spec and -32000 to -32019 to implementations. A server that uses a reserved code, or an integer-less one, breaks clients that switch on error codes.

**How to fix.** Use the standard JSON-RPC codes, the spec-defined -32020 to -32022, or a code in -32000..-32019. Report a missing resource as -32602 in the modern era.

### protocol.result_type_present

**Every modern result carries resultType**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#result

**Why it matters.** resultType tells a client whether a result is complete or needs more input. Without it, clients cannot tell a finished result from an input request.

**How to fix.** Include resultType ("complete" or "input_required") in every result.

### protocol.stdout_clean

**Standard output carries only MCP messages**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio

**Why it matters.** On stdio, stdout is the protocol channel. A stray print or banner there corrupts the stream for every client.

**How to fix.** Write logs and diagnostics to stderr; keep stdout for JSON-RPC messages only.

### schema.cache_fields_present

**Cacheable results carry ttlMs and cacheScope**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** Clients and gateways decide how long to reuse a list and whether to share it between users from ttlMs and cacheScope. Without them they guess, and may serve one user's list to another.

**How to fix.** Add ttlMs (a non-negative number) and cacheScope (public or private) to list, read and discover results.
